newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Oct CPI rose 1.25 percent - Banco de Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Oct CPI rose 1.25 percent - Banco de Mexico.

text.p: Mexico's consumer price index rose 1.25 percent in October from the month before after rising 1.60 percent in September, Banco de Mexico said.
The central bank added that the producer price index rose 1.20 percent in October from the month before, compared to rise of 1.03 percent in September.
The central bank said that compared with the same month a year earlier the CPI was 28.97 percent higher.
It said the monthly rate of consumer inflation during October was the lowest in the last 22 months.
The accumulated inflation rate for the first ten months of the year was 21.90 percent, compared with 43.63 percent in the same period a year earlier.

It said that the main causes of inflation this year was an increase in prices of domestic electricity use, soft drinks, automobiles, long-distance telephone charges, fruits and vegetables, and other products.
It said that the basic basket of consumer goods rose 1.53 percent in October from the month before.
A survey of 10 Mexican brokerages and research companies found expectations of a rise of 1.31 percent for October's CPI.
Banco de Mexico gave the following breakdown for October:
INDEX Percent
Food, drinks and tobacco 1.09
Clothing and shoes 1.50
Housing 2.05
Furniture 1.29
Health and personal care 1.11
Transportation 0.94
Education 0.49
Other services 0.90
In October, the producer price index, excluding petroleum, was 27.79 percent higher than the same month a year earlier.
The accumulated increase for the first ten months was 19.63 percent.
In the first ten months of 1995, the index rose an accumulated 46.88 percent, Banco de Mexico said.
